nodes.name: Path of Subgraph
nodes.description:
Returns the path identifying the subgraph (network) that contains this proto node — i.e. the input `node_path`
with its own trailing entry dropped. The terminating element of the returned path is the document node whose
encapsulated network we live in, so the path doubles as a unique reference to that node at any nesting depth.
Used as the value source for stamping the `editor:layer_path` attribute on each item of a layer's output, which lets
editor tools (e.g. selection, click target routing) trace data back to its owning layer regardless of whether
the layer is at the root document network or nested inside a custom subgraph.

nodes.name: Regex Find
nodes.description:
Finds a regex match in the string and returns its components. The result is a list where the first item is the whole match (`$0`) and subsequent items are the capture groups (`$1`, `$2`, etc., if any).

The match index selects which non-overlapping occurrence to return (0 for the first match). Returns an empty list if no match is found at the given index.

Each item carries `start` and `end` byte-offset attributes pointing into the original string, plus a `name` attribute holding
the capture group's name (empty for unnamed groups, and for index 0 which is the whole match).

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to search within.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The regular expression pattern to search for.

inputs.name: match_index
inputs.description: Which non-overlapping occurrence of the pattern to return, starting from 0 for the first match. Negative indices count backwards from the last match.

inputs.name: case_insensitive
inputs.description: Match letters regardless of case.

inputs.name: multiline
inputs.description: Make `^` and `$` match the start and end of each line, not just the whole string.

inputs.rust_type: impl Node<Context<'static>, Output = RenderOutput> + Send + Sync

inputs.rust_type: impl Node<Context<'static>, Output = RenderOutput> + Send + Sync

nodes.name: Attach Attribute
nodes.description:
Sets a named attribute on the primary list, with each value taken from the corresponding item's element in the source list (paired by index, wrapping if the source has fewer items).
The source is type-erased into an `AttributeDyn` by an auto-inserted convert node, so this node only monomorphizes over `T` instead of the cartesian product `(T, U)`.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The `List` to attach the new attribute to.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: The source values to attach.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The name to assign to the new destination attribute.

nodes.name: Write Attribute
nodes.description:
Sets a named attribute on the input `List`, computing one value per item via the value-producing input. That input
is evaluated once per item, with the item's index and the item itself (as a `List` containing only that item,
passed as a vararg) provided via context, so the upstream pipeline can return a different value per item that may
be derived from the item's own data. If the attribute already exists, its values are replaced; if not, it's added.
The value is type-erased into an `AttributeValueDyn` by an auto-inserted convert node, so this node only
monomorphizes over `T` instead of the cartesian product `(T, U)`.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The `List` to set the named attribute on (one value per item).

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The attribute name (key) to write or replace.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The node that produces the attribute value for each item. Called once per item with the item's index in context.

nodes.name: Blend Mode
nodes.description: Applies the blend mode to the input graphics. Setting this allows for customizing how overlapping content is composited together.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The layer stack that will be composited when rendering.

inputs.name: blend_mode
inputs.description: The choice of equation that controls how brightness and color blends between overlapping pixels.

nodes.name: Clipping Mask
nodes.description: Sets whether the input graphics inherit the alpha of the content beneath them, "clipping" them to that content.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The layer stack that will be composited when rendering.

inputs.name: clip
inputs.description: Whether the content inherits the alpha of the content beneath it.

nodes.name: Opacity
nodes.description:
Modifies the opacity and/or fill of the input graphics by multiplying the existing values by these percentages.
Opacity affects the transparency of the content (together with anything above which is clipped to it).
Fill affects the transparency of the content itself, independent of any content clipped to it.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The layer stack that will be composited when rendering.

inputs.name: has_opacity
inputs.description: Whether the *Opacity* property is enabled, multiplying the existing opacity by the chosen percentage.

inputs.name: opacity
inputs.description:
How visible the content should be, including any content clipped to it.
Ranges from the default of 100% (fully opaque) to 0% (fully transparent).

inputs.name: has_fill
inputs.description: Whether the *Fill* property is enabled, multiplying the existing fill by the chosen percentage.

inputs.name: fill
inputs.description:
How visible the content should be, independent of any content clipped to it.
Ranges from 0% (fully transparent) to the default of 100% (fully opaque).

nodes.name: Colors To Gradient
nodes.description: Constructs a gradient from a `Color[]`, where the colors are evenly distributed as gradient stops across the range from 0 to 1.

nodes.name: Gradient Type
nodes.description: Sets the type (linear or radial) of each gradient in the input list.

nodes.name: HSLA to Color
nodes.description: Constructs a color value from hue, saturation, lightness, and alpha components given as numbers from 0 to 1.

nodes.name: HSVA to Color
nodes.description: Constructs a color value from hue, saturation, value, and alpha components given as numbers from 0 to 1.

nodes.name: Hex to Color
nodes.description: Constructs a color value from a CSS color string. Accepts hex (`#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBBAA`, plus bare and shorthand variants), CSS named colors (like `red`), and functional notations (`rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)`, etc.). Invalid inputs produce no color.

nodes.name: RGBA to Color
nodes.description: Constructs a color value from red, green, blue, and alpha components given as numbers from 0 to 1.

nodes.name: Sample Gradient
nodes.description: Gets the color at the specified position along the gradient, given a position from 0 (left) to 1 (right).

nodes.name: Spread Method
nodes.description: Sets how each gradient in the input list extends past its endpoints: Pad, Reflect, or Repeat.

nodes.name: Read Index
nodes.description:
Produces the index of the current iteration of a loop by reading from the evaluation context, which is supplied by downstream nodes such as *Repeat*.

Nested loops can enable 2D or higher-dimensional iteration by using the *Loop Level* parameter to read the index from outer levels of loops.

inputs.name: loop_level
inputs.description:
The number of nested loops to traverse outwards (from the innermost loop) to get the index from. The most upstream loop is level 0, and downstream loops add levels.
In programming terms: inside the double loop `i { j { ... } }`, *Loop Level* 0 = `j` and 1 = `i`. After inserting a third loop `k { ... }`, inside it, levels would be 0 = `k`, 1 = `j`, and 2 = `i`.

inputs.name: loop_level
inputs.description:
The number of nested loops to traverse outwards (from the innermost loop) to get the position from. The most upstream loop is level 0, and downstream loops add levels.
In programming terms: inside the double loop `i { j { ... } }`, *Loop Level* 0 = `j` and 1 = `i`. After inserting a third loop `k { ... }`, inside it, levels would be 0 = `k`, 1 = `j`, and 2 = `i`.

nodes.name: Read String
nodes.description: Reads the current string from within a **Map String** node's loop.

nodes.name: As String
nodes.description: Type-asserts a value to be a string.

nodes.name: As f64
nodes.description: Convert an integer to a decimal number of the type f64, which may be the required type for certain node inputs.

nodes.name: As u32
nodes.description: Convert a number to an integer of the type u32, which may be the required type for certain node inputs.

nodes.name: As u64
nodes.description: Convert a number to an integer of the type u64, which may be the required type for certain node inputs.

nodes.name: Clone
nodes.description: Meant for debugging purposes, not general use. Clones the input value.

nodes.name: Log to Console
nodes.description: Meant for debugging purposes, not general use. Logs the input value to the console and passes it through unchanged.

nodes.name: Serialize
nodes.description: Converts a value to a JSON string representation.

nodes.name: Size Of
nodes.description: Meant for debugging purposes, not general use. Returns the size of the input type in bytes.

nodes.name: Some
nodes.description: Meant for debugging purposes, not general use. Wraps the input value in the Some variant of an Option.

nodes.name: Unwrap Option
nodes.description: Meant for debugging purposes, not general use. Unwraps the input value from an Option, returning the default value if the input is None.

nodes.name: Extend
nodes.description: Joins two `List`s of the same type, extending the base `List` with the items from the new `List`.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The `List` whose items will appear at the start of the extended `List`.

inputs.name: new
inputs.description: The `List` whose items will appear at the end of the extended `List`.

nodes.name: Extract Element
nodes.description:
Returns the bare element (without the item's attributes) at the specified index in a `List`.
Use this when downstream nodes want just the inner value rather than a `List` containing a single item.
If no value exists at that index, the element type's default is returned.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The `List` of data to extract from.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the item to retrieve, starting from 0 for the first item. Negative indices count backwards from the end of the list, starting from -1 for the last item.

nodes.name: Flatten Color
nodes.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `Color[]` by deeply flattening any color content it contains, and discarding any non-color content.

nodes.name: Flatten Gradient
nodes.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `GradientStops[]` by deeply flattening any gradient content it contains, and discarding any non-gradient content.

nodes.name: Flatten Graphic
nodes.description: Removes a level of nesting from a `Graphic[]`, or all nesting if "Fully Flatten" is enabled.

nodes.name: Index Elements
nodes.description:
Returns the value at the specified index in the list.
If no value exists at that index, the type's default value is returned.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of data.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the item to retrieve, starting from 0 for the first item. Negative indices count backwards from the end of the list, starting from -1 for the last item.

nodes.name: Memoize
nodes.description:
Helps speed up repeated renders in a computationally-heavy part of the node graph.

Stores the last evaluated data that flowed through this node and immediately returns that data on subsequent renders if the context has not changed.

inputs.name: input
inputs.rust_type: I, #[data] cache: Arc<Mutex<Option<(u64, T)>>>, content: impl Node<I, Output = T>

nodes.name: Omit Element
nodes.description:
Returns the list with the element at the specified index removed.
If no value exists at that index, the list is returned unchanged.

inputs.name: list
inputs.description: The list of data.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the item to remove, starting from 0 for the first item. Negative indices count backwards from the end of the list, starting from -1 for the last item.

nodes.name: Passthrough
nodes.description: Passes-through the input value without changing it. This is useful for rerouting wires for organization purposes.

nodes.name: To Graphic
nodes.description:
Converts a list of graphical content into a `Graphic[]` by placing it into an element of a new wrapper `Graphic[]`.
If it is already a `Graphic[]`, it is not wrapped again. Use the 'Wrap Graphic' node if wrapping is always desired.

nodes.name: Wrap Graphic
nodes.description:
Nests the input graphical content in a wrapper graphic. This essentially "groups" the input.
The inverse of this node is 'Flatten Graphic'.

nodes.name: Add
nodes.description: The addition operation (`+`) calculates the sum of two scalar numbers or vectors.

inputs.name: augend
inputs.description: The left-hand side of the addition operation.

inputs.name: addend
inputs.description: The right-hand side of the addition operation.

nodes.name: Divide
nodes.description:
The division operation (`÷`) calculates the quotient of two scalar numbers or vectors.

Produces 0 if the denominator is 0.

inputs.name: numerator
inputs.description: The left-hand side of the division operation.

inputs.name: denominator
inputs.description: The right-hand side of the division operation.

nodes.name: Exponent
nodes.description: The exponent operation (`^`) calculates the result of raising a number to a power.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The base number that is raised to the power.

inputs.name: power
inputs.description: The power to which the base number is raised.

nodes.name: Logarithm
nodes.description: The logarithmic function (`log`) calculates the logarithm of a number with a specified base. If the natural logarithm function (`ln`) is desired, set the base to "e".

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number for which the logarithm is calculated.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The base of the logarithm, such as 2 (binary), 10 (decimal), and e (natural logarithm).

nodes.name: Math
nodes.description: Calculates a mathematical expression with input values "A" and "B".

inputs.name: operand_a
inputs.description: The value of "A" when calculating the expression.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: A math expression that may incorporate "A" and/or "B", such as `sqrt(A + B) - B^2`.

inputs.name: operand_b
inputs.description: The value of "B" when calculating the expression.

nodes.name: Modulo
nodes.description:
The modulo operation (`%`) calculates the remainder from the division of two scalar numbers or vectors.

The sign of the result shares the sign of the numerator unless *Always Positive* is enabled.

inputs.name: numerator
inputs.description: The left-hand side of the modulo operation.

inputs.name: modulus
inputs.description: The right-hand side of the modulo operation.

inputs.name: always_positive
inputs.description: Ensures the result is always positive, even if the numerator is negative.

nodes.name: Multiply
nodes.description: The multiplication operation (`×`) calculates the product of two scalar numbers, vectors, or transforms.

inputs.name: multiplier
inputs.description: The left-hand side of the multiplication operation.

inputs.name: multiplicand
inputs.description: The right-hand side of the multiplication operation.

nodes.name: Reciprocal
nodes.description:
The reciprocal operation (`1/x`) calculates the multiplicative inverse of a number.

Produces 0 if the input is 0.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number for which the reciprocal is calculated.

nodes.name: Root
nodes.description:
The `n`th root operation (`√`) calculates the inverse of exponentiation. Square root inverts squaring, cube root inverts cubing, and so on.

This is equivalent to raising the number to the power of `1/n`.

inputs.name: radicand
inputs.description: The number inside the radical for which the `n`th root is calculated.

inputs.name: degree
inputs.description:
The degree of the root to be calculated. Square root is 2, cube root is 3, and so on.
Degrees 0 or less are invalid and will produce an output of 0.

nodes.name: Subtract
nodes.description: The subtraction operation (`-`) calculates the difference between two scalar numbers or vectors.

inputs.name: minuend
inputs.description: The left-hand side of the subtraction operation.

inputs.name: subtrahend
inputs.description: The right-hand side of the subtraction operation.

nodes.name: Equals
nodes.description: The equality operation (`==`, `XNOR`) compares two values and returns true if they are equal, or false if they are not.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two values to compare for equality.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two values to compare for equality.

nodes.name: Greater Than
nodes.description:
The greater-than operation (`>`) compares two values and returns true if the first value is greater than the second, or false if it is not.
If enabled with *Or Equal*, the greater-than-or-equal operation (`>=`) is used instead.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number on the left-hand side of the comparison.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The number on the right-hand side of the comparison.

inputs.name: or_equal
inputs.description: Uses the greater-than-or-equal operation (`>=`) instead of the greater-than operation (`>`).

nodes.name: Less Than
nodes.description:
The less-than operation (`<`) compares two values and returns true if the first value is less than the second, or false if it is not.
If enabled with *Or Equal*, the less-than-or-equal operation (`<=`) is used instead.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number on the left-hand side of the comparison.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The number on the right-hand side of the comparison.

inputs.name: or_equal
inputs.description: Uses the less-than-or-equal operation (`<=`) instead of the less-than operation (`<`).

nodes.name: Logical And
nodes.description: The logical AND operation (`&&`) returns true if both of the two inputs are true, or false if any are false.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two boolean values, both of which must be true for the node to output true.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two boolean values, both of which must be true for the node to output true.

nodes.name: Logical Not
nodes.description: The logical NOT operation (`!`) reverses true and false value of the input.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: The boolean value to be reversed.

nodes.name: Logical Or
nodes.description: The logical OR operation (`||`) returns true if either of the two inputs are true, or false if both are false.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two boolean values, either of which may be true for the node to output true.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two boolean values, either of which may be true for the node to output true.

nodes.name: Not Equals
nodes.description: The inequality operation (`!=`, `XOR`) compares two values and returns true if they are not equal, or false if they are.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two values to compare for inequality.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two values to compare for inequality.

nodes.name: Switch
nodes.description: Evaluates either the "If True" or "If False" input branch based on whether the input condition is true or false.

nodes.name: Absolute Value
nodes.description: The absolute value function (`abs`) removes the negative sign from an input value, if present.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number to be made positive.

nodes.name: Ceiling
nodes.description: The ceiling function (`ceil`) rounds up an input value to the nearest whole number, unless the input number is already whole.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number to be rounded up.

nodes.name: Clamp
nodes.description: The clamp function (`clamp`) restricts a number to a specified range between a minimum and maximum value. The minimum and maximum values are automatically swapped if they are reversed.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number to be clamped, which is restricted to the range between the minimum and maximum values.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: The left (smaller) side of the range. The output is never less than this number.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: The right (greater) side of the range. The output is never greater than this number.

nodes.name: Floor
nodes.description: The floor function (`floor`) rounds down an input value to the nearest whole number, unless the input number is already whole.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number to be rounded down.

nodes.name: Greatest Common Divisor
nodes.description: The greatest common divisor (GCD) calculates the largest positive integer that divides both of the two input numbers without leaving a remainder.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two numbers for which the GCD is calculated.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two numbers for which the GCD is calculated.

nodes.name: Least Common Multiple
nodes.description: The least common multiple (LCM) calculates the smallest positive integer that is a multiple of both of the two input numbers.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two numbers for which the LCM is calculated.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two numbers for which the LCM is calculated.

nodes.name: Max
nodes.description: The maximum function (`max`) picks the larger of two numbers.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two numbers, of which the greater is returned.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two numbers, of which the greater is returned.

nodes.name: Min
nodes.description: The minimum function (`min`) picks the smaller of two numbers.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: One of the two numbers, of which the lesser is returned.

inputs.name: other_value
inputs.description: The other of the two numbers, of which the lesser is returned.

nodes.name: Random
nodes.description: The random function (`rand`) converts a seed into a random number within the specified range, inclusive of the minimum and exclusive of the maximum. The minimum and maximum values are automatically swapped if they are reversed.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Seed to determine the unique variation of which number is generated.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: The smaller end of the range within which the random number is generated.

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: The larger end of the range within which the random number is generated.

nodes.name: Remap
nodes.description:
Linearly maps an input value from one range to another. The ranges may be reversed.

For example, 0.5 in the input range `[0, 1]` would map to 0 in the output range `[-180, 180]`.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The value to be mapped between ranges.

inputs.name: input_min
inputs.description: The lower bound of the input range.

inputs.name: input_max
inputs.description: The upper bound of the input range.

inputs.name: output_min
inputs.description: The lower bound of the output range.

inputs.name: output_max
inputs.description: The upper bound of the output range.

inputs.name: clamped
inputs.description: Whether to constrain the result within the output range instead of extrapolating beyond its bounds.

nodes.name: Round
nodes.description: The rounding function (`round`) maps an input value to its nearest whole number. Halfway values are rounded away from zero.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The number to be rounded to the nearest whole number.

nodes.name: Decompose Rotation
nodes.description: Extracts the rotation component (in degrees) from the input transform.

nodes.name: Decompose Scale
nodes.description:
Extracts the scale component from the input transform.
**Magnitude** returns the visual length of each axis (always positive, includes any skew contribution).
**Pure** returns the isolated scale factors with rotation and skew stripped away (can be negative for flipped axes).

nodes.name: Decompose Skew
nodes.description: Extracts the skew angle (in degrees) from the input transform.

nodes.name: Decompose Translation
nodes.description: Extracts the translation component from the input transform.

nodes.name: Extract Transform
nodes.description: Obtains the transform of the first item in the input `List`, if present.

nodes.name: Invert Transform
nodes.description: Produces the inverse of the input transform, which is the transform that undoes the effect of the original transform.

nodes.name: Replace Transform
nodes.description: Overwrites the transform of each item in the input `List` with the specified transform.

nodes.name: Reset Transform
nodes.description:
Resets the desired components of the input transform to their default values. If all components are reset, the output will be set to the identity transform.
Shear is represented jointly by rotation and scale, so resetting both will also remove any shear.

nodes.name: Transform
nodes.description: Applies the specified transform to the input value, which may be a graphic type or another transform.

nodes.name: Cosine
nodes.description: The cosine trigonometric function (`cos`) calculates the ratio of the angle's adjacent side length to its hypotenuse length.

inputs.name: theta
inputs.description: The given angle.

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the given angle should be interpreted as radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Cosine Inverse
nodes.description: The inverse cosine trigonometric function (`acos`) calculates the angle whose cosine is the input value.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The given value for which the angle is calculated. Must be in the domain `[-1, 1]` (it will be clamped to -1 or 1 otherwise).

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Sine
nodes.description: The sine trigonometric function (`sin`) calculates the ratio of the angle's opposite side length to its hypotenuse length.

inputs.name: theta
inputs.description: The given angle.

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the given angle should be interpreted as radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Sine Inverse
nodes.description: The inverse sine trigonometric function (`asin`) calculates the angle whose sine is the input value.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The given value for which the angle is calculated. Must be in the domain `[-1, 1]` (it will be clamped to -1 or 1 otherwise).

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Tangent
nodes.description: The tangent trigonometric function (`tan`) calculates the ratio of the angle's opposite side length to its adjacent side length.

inputs.name: theta
inputs.description: The given angle.

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the given angle should be interpreted as radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Tangent Inverse
nodes.description:
The inverse tangent trigonometric function (`atan` or `atan2`, depending on input type) calculates:
`atan`: the angle whose tangent is the input scalar number.
`atan2`: the angle of a ray from the origin to the input vec2.

The resulting angle is always in the range `[-90°, 90°]` or, in radians, `[-π/2, π/2]`.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The given value for which the angle is calculated.

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Angle Between
nodes.description:
Calculates the angle swept between two vectors.

The value is always positive and ranges from 0° (both vectors point the same direction) to 180° (both vectors point opposite directions).

nodes.name: Angle To
nodes.description: Calculates the angle needed for a rightward-facing object placed at the observer position to turn so it points toward the target position.

inputs.name: observer
inputs.description: The position from which the angle is measured.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The position toward which the angle is measured.

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Dot Product
nodes.description:
The dot product operation (`·`) calculates the degree of similarity of a vec2 pair based on their angles and lengths.

Calculated as `‖a‖‖b‖cos(θ)`, it represents the product of their lengths (`‖a‖‖b‖`) scaled by the alignment of their directions (`cos(θ)`).
The output ranges from the positive to negative product of their lengths based on when they are pointing in the same or opposite directions.
If any vector has zero length, the output is 0.

inputs.name: vector_a
inputs.description: An operand of the dot product operation.

inputs.name: vector_b
inputs.description: The other operand of the dot product operation.

inputs.name: normalize
inputs.description: Whether to normalize both input vectors so the calculation ranges in `[-1, 1]` by considering only their degree of directional alignment.

nodes.name: Extract XY
nodes.description:
Obtains the X or Y component of a vec2.

The inverse of this node is "Vec2 Value", which can have either or both its X and Y parameters exposed as graph inputs.

nodes.name: Length
nodes.description: The magnitude operator (`‖x‖`) calculates the length of a vec2, which is the distance from the base to the tip of the arrow represented by the vector.

nodes.name: Normalize
nodes.description:
Scales the input vector to unit length while preserving its direction. This is equivalent to dividing the input vector by its own magnitude.

Returns 0 when the input vector has zero length.

nodes.name: Brush
nodes.description:
Generates the brush strokes painted with the Brush tool as a raster image.
If an input image is supplied, strokes are drawn on top of it, expanding bounds as needed.

inputs.name: background
inputs.description: Optional raster content that may be drawn onto.

inputs.name: trace
inputs.description: The list of brush stroke paths drawn by the Brush tool, with each including both its coordinates and styles.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Internal cache data used to accelerate rendering of the brush content.

nodes.name: Flatten Raster
nodes.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `Raster[]` by deeply flattening any raster content it contains, and discarding any non-raster content.

inputs.name: image
inputs.description: The image to be masked.

inputs.name: stencil
inputs.description: The stencil to be used for masking.

nodes.name: Blur
nodes.description: Blurs the image with a Gaussian or box blur kernel filter.

inputs.name: image_frame
inputs.description: The image to be blurred.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: The radius of the blur kernel.

inputs.name: box_blur
inputs.description: Use a lower-quality box kernel instead of a circular Gaussian kernel. This is faster but produces boxy artifacts.

inputs.name: gamma
inputs.description: Opt to incorrectly apply the filter with color calculations in gamma space for compatibility with the results from other software.

nodes.name: Median Filter
nodes.description: Applies a median filter to reduce noise while preserving edges.

inputs.name: image_frame
inputs.description: The image to be filtered.

inputs.name: radius
inputs.description: The radius of the filter kernel. Larger values remove more noise but may blur fine details.

nodes.name: Noise Pattern
nodes.description: Generates customizable procedural noise patterns.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Artwork to be copied and placed at each point.

inputs.name: random_scale_min
inputs.description: Minimum range of randomized sizes given to each placed copy.

inputs.name: random_scale_max
inputs.description: Maximum range of randomized sizes given to each placed copy.

inputs.name: random_scale_bias
inputs.description: Bias for the probability distribution of randomized sizes (0 is uniform, negatives favor more of small sizes, positives favor more of large sizes).

inputs.name: random_scale_seed
inputs.description: Seed to determine unique variations on all the randomized copy sizes.

inputs.name: random_rotation
inputs.description: Range of randomized angles given to each placed copy, in degrees ranging from furthest clockwise to counterclockwise.

inputs.name: random_rotation_seed
inputs.description: Seed to determine unique variations on all the randomized copy angles.

nodes.name: Format Number
nodes.description: Formats a number as a string with control over decimal places, decimal separator, and thousands grouping.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The number to format as a string.

inputs.name: decimal_places
inputs.description: The amount of digits after the decimal point. The value is rounded to fit. Set to 0 to show only whole numbers.

inputs.name: decimal_separator
inputs.description: The character(s) used as the decimal point.

inputs.name: fixed_decimals
inputs.description: Always show the exact number of decimal places, even if they are trailing zeros.

inputs.name: use_thousands_separator
inputs.description: Whether to group digits with a thousands separator.

inputs.name: thousands_separator
inputs.description: The character(s) inserted between digit groups.

inputs.name: start_at_10000
inputs.description: Don't group 4-digit numbers with a thousands separator (only start grouping at 10,000 and above).

nodes.name: Map String
nodes.description: Iterates over a list of strings, evaluating the mapped operation for each one. Use the **Read String** node to access the current string inside the loop.

nodes.name: String Capitalization
nodes.description: Converts a string's capitalization style to another of the common upper and lower case patterns, optionally joining words with a chosen separator.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to have its letter capitalization converted.

inputs.name: capitalization
inputs.description: The capitalization style to apply.

inputs.name: use_joiner
inputs.description: Whether to split the string into words and reconnect with the chosen joiner. When disabled, the existing word structure separators are preserved.

inputs.name: joiner
inputs.description: The string placed between each word.

nodes.name: String Concatenate
nodes.description: Joins two strings together.

nodes.name: String Contains
nodes.description: Checks whether the string contains the given substring. Optionally restricts the match to only the start and/or end of the string.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to search within.

inputs.name: substring
inputs.description: The substring to search for.

inputs.name: at_start
inputs.description: Only match if the substring appears at the start of the string.

inputs.name: at_end
inputs.description: Only match if the substring appears at the end of the string.

nodes.name: String Escape
nodes.description:
Converts between literal escape sequences and their corresponding control characters within a string.

Unescape: `\n` (newline), `\r` (carriage return), `\t` (tab), `\0` (null), and `\\` (backslash) are converted into the actual special characters.
Escape: the actual special characters are converted back into their escape sequence representations.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string that contains either literal escape sequences or control characters to be converted to the opposite representation.

inputs.name: unescape
inputs.description: Convert the control characters back into their escape sequence representations.

nodes.name: String Find Index
nodes.description: Similar to the **String Contains** node, this searches within the input string for the first (or last) occurrence of a substring and returns the index of where that begins, or -1 if not found.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to search within.

inputs.name: substring
inputs.description: The substring to search for.

inputs.name: from_end
inputs.description: Find the start index of the last occurrence instead of the first.

nodes.name: String Join
nodes.description:
Joins a list of strings together with a separator between each pair. This is the inverse of the **String Split** node.

For example, joining `["a", "b", "c"]` with separator ", " produces "a, b, c".

inputs.name: strings
inputs.description: The list of strings to join together.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: The text placed between each pair of strings.

inputs.name: separator_escaping
inputs.description:
Whether to convert escape sequences found in the separator into their corresponding characters:
"\n" (newline), "\r" (carriage return), "\t" (tab), "\0" (null), and "\\" (backslash).

nodes.name: String Length
nodes.description: Counts the number of characters in a string.

nodes.name: String Occurrences
nodes.description: Counts the number of occurrences of a substring within the string.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to search within.

inputs.name: substring
inputs.description: The substring to count occurrences of.

inputs.name: overlapping
inputs.description:
Whether to count overlapping occurrences, using the substring as a sliding window.
For example, "aa" occurs twice in "aaaa" without overlapping but three times with overlapping.

nodes.name: String Pad
nodes.description: Pads the string to a target length by filling with the given repeated substring. If the string already meets or exceeds the target length, it is returned unchanged.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to be padded to a target length.

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: The target character length after padding. When "Up To" is set, this length concerns only the portion before (or after) that substring.

inputs.name: padding
inputs.description: The repeated substring used to fill the remaining space. A multi-charcter substring may end partway through its final repetition.

inputs.name: up_to
inputs.description:
Pad only the length of the string encountered before the start of the first (or after the end of the last) occurrence of this substring, if given and present (otherwise the full string is considered).
For example, this can pad numbers with leading zeros to align them before the decimal point.

inputs.name: from_end
inputs.description: Pad at the end of the string instead of the start.

nodes.name: String Repeat
nodes.description: Repeats the string a given number of times, optionally with a separator between each repetition.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to be repeated.

inputs.name: count
inputs.description: The number of times the string should appear in the output.

inputs.name: separator
inputs.description: The string placed between each repetition.

inputs.name: separator_escaping
inputs.description:
Whether to convert escape sequences found in the separator into their corresponding characters:
"\n" (newline), "\r" (carriage return), "\t" (tab), "\0" (null), and "\\" (backslash).

nodes.name: String Replace
nodes.description: Replaces all occurrences of "From" with "To" in the input string.

nodes.name: String Reverse
nodes.description: Reverses the sequence of characters making up the string so it reads back-to-front. ("Backwards text" becomes "txet sdrawkcaB".)

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to be reversed.

nodes.name: String Slice
nodes.description:
Extracts a substring from the input string, starting at "Start" and ending before "End".

Negative indices count from the end of the string. If the index of "Start" equals or exceeds "End", the result is an empty string.

nodes.name: String Split
nodes.description:
Splits a string into a list of substrings based on the specified delimiter. This is the inverse of the **String Join** node.

For example, splitting "a, b, c" with delimiter ", " produces `["a", "b", "c"]`.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to split into substrings.

inputs.name: delimiter
inputs.description: The character(s) that separate the substrings. These are not included in the outputs.

inputs.name: delimiter_escaping
inputs.description:
Whether to convert escape sequences found in the delimiter into their corresponding characters:
"\n" (newline), "\r" (carriage return), "\t" (tab), "\0" (null), and "\\" (backslash).

nodes.name: String To Number
nodes.description: Parses a string into a number. Falls back to the chosen value if the string is not a valid number.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string containing a number. Surrounding whitespace is ignored, a decimal point (.) may be included, sign prefixes (+/-) are respected, and scientific notation (e.g. "1e-3") is supported.

inputs.name: fallback
inputs.description: The value of the result if the string cannot be parsed as a valid number.

nodes.name: String Trim
nodes.description: Removes leading and/or trailing whitespace from a string. Common whitespace characters include spaces, tabs, and newlines.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string that may contain leading and trailing whitespace that should be removed.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Whether the start of the string should have its whitespace removed.

inputs.name: end
inputs.description: Whether the end of the string should have its whitespace removed.

nodes.name: String Truncate
nodes.description: Clips the string to a maximum character length, optionally appending a suffix (like "…") when truncation occurs. Strings already within the limit are not modified.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to truncate.

inputs.name: length
inputs.description: The maximum number of characters allowed, including the suffix if one is appended.

inputs.name: suffix
inputs.description: A suffix appended to indicate truncation occurred, unless empty. Its length counts towards the character budget.

nodes.name: Text
nodes.description:
Produces a styled `String[]` carrying all typographic attributes.

Use the **Text to Vector** node to convert this into vector geometry if desired.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text content to be drawn.

inputs.name: font
inputs.description: The loaded font file used to draw the text. The editor resolves the chosen typeface to these bytes via the resource system.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: The font size used to draw the text.

inputs.name: line_height
inputs.description:
The line height ratio, relative to the font size. Each line is drawn lower than its previous line by the distance of *Size* × *Line Height*.
0 means all lines overlap. 1 means all lines are spaced by just the font size. 1.2 is a common default for readable text. 2 means double-spaced text.

inputs.name: letter_spacing
inputs.description: Additional spacing, in pixels, added between each character.

inputs.name: letter_tilt
inputs.description: The angle of faux italic slant applied to each glyph.

inputs.name: has_max_width
inputs.description: Enables the maximum width constraint so lines can wrap.

inputs.name: max_width
inputs.description: The maximum width that the text block can occupy before wrapping to a new line. Otherwise, lines do not wrap.

inputs.name: has_max_height
inputs.description: Whether the *Max Height* property is enabled so that lines beyond it are not drawn.

inputs.name: max_height
inputs.description: The maximum height that the text block can occupy. Excess lines are not drawn.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: The horizontal alignment of each line of text within its surrounding box. To have an effect on a single line of text, *Max Width* must be set.

nodes.name: Text to Vector
nodes.description: Converts a styled `String[]` into vector geometry.

inputs.name: strings
inputs.description: A styled list of text strings produced by the **Text** node (or any other `String[]` source).

inputs.name: separate_glyphs
inputs.description: Whether to split every letterform into its own vector item. Otherwise, a single vector compound path is produced.

nodes.name: Format JSON
nodes.description: Reformats a JSON string with control over indentation, line breaking, and spacing. Trailing commas are tolerated. Otherwise-invalid JSON input is returned unchanged.

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: The JSON string to reformat.

inputs.name: compact
inputs.description: Removes optional spaces within curly brackets and after colons and commas.

inputs.name: multi_line
inputs.description: Break arrays and objects across multiple lines when they exceed the line break length.

inputs.name: indent
inputs.description: The indentation string used for each nesting level. Escape sequences like `\t` (the tab character) are supported. Two or four spaces are also common choices.

inputs.name: break_length
inputs.description:
The maximum line length before a container (array or object) is broken across lines. Set this to 0 to always break containers. (Requires *Multi-Line* to take effect.)
This is not a maximum line length guarantee. Deep nesting and long keys or values may exceed this length.

inputs.name: break_nested
inputs.description: Always break a container (array or object) across lines if it holds another container, even if it would fit within the break length. (Requires *Multi-Line* to take effect.)

nodes.name: Query JSON
nodes.description:
Extracts a single matched value from a JSON string using a path expression (see that parameter's description for its syntax). If no matches are found, an empty string is returned. If multiple values are matched, the first is returned. To read all matches, use the **Query JSON All** node.

This is useful in conjunction with the nodes:
• **String to Number**: convert numeric query results to numbers.
• **String Value** → **Equals**: convert "true", "false", or "null" query results to bools.

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: The JSON string to extract a value from.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description:
Determines which contained value to extract from within the JSON.
The path syntax is like JavaScript's accessor syntax that follows an array/object value. It also supports negative indexing to count backwards from the end. Additionally, `[]` accesses all array and object values instead of just one.
Examples:
Use `[2]` or `[-1]` to get the last value, and `[1]` or `[-2]` for the middle value, of `["a", "b", "c"]`.
Use `.size` or `["size"]` to get the `size` property of `{ "size": 10 }`. The latter form is required if the key contains spaces or special characters like `["this key with spaces!"]`.
Use chained accessors like `.fonts[0].name` to query deeper.
Use the `[]` accessor to query all elements, like `.fonts[].weights[]` to get every weight of every font.

inputs.name: unquote_strings
inputs.description: Strips the surrounding double quotes from string values, returning the raw text. Other types are never wrapped in quotes.

nodes.name: Query JSON All
nodes.description:
Extracts every matched value from a JSON string using a path expression (see that parameter's description for its syntax). A list of zero or more resultant strings is produced. The `[]` path accessor is used to read more than one value.

Each item carries a `type` attribute holding the matched value's JSON type (`"string"`, `"number"`, `"bool"`, `"null"`, `"object"`, or `"array"`).

This is useful in conjunction with the nodes:
• **Index Elements**: access the `N`th query result.
• **String to Number**: convert numeric query results to numbers.
• **String Value** → **Equals**: convert "true", "false", or "null" query results to bools.

inputs.name: json
inputs.description: The JSON string to extract values from.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description:
Determines which contained values to extract from within the JSON.
The path syntax is like JavaScript's accessor syntax that follows an array/object value. It also supports negative indexing to count backwards from the end. Additionally, `[]` accesses all array and object values instead of just one.
Examples:
Use `[2]` or `[-1]` to get the last value, and `[1]` or `[-2]` for the middle value, of `["a", "b", "c"]`.
Use `.size` or `["size"]` to get the `size` property of `{ "size": 10 }`. The latter form is required if the key contains spaces or special characters like `["this key with spaces!"]`.
Use chained accessors like `.fonts[0].name` to query deeper.
Use the `[]` accessor to query all elements, like `.fonts[].weights[]` to get every weight of every font.

inputs.name: unquote_strings
inputs.description: Strips the surrounding double quotes from string values, returning the raw text. Other types are never wrapped in quotes.

nodes.name: Regex Contains
nodes.description: Checks whether the string contains a match for the given regular expression pattern. Optionally restricts the match to only the start and/or end of the string.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to search within.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The regular expression pattern to search for.

inputs.name: case_insensitive
inputs.description: Match letters regardless of case.

inputs.name: multiline
inputs.description: Make `^` and `$` match the start and end of each line, not just the whole string.

inputs.name: at_start
inputs.description: Only match if the pattern appears at the start of the string.

inputs.name: at_end
inputs.description: Only match if the pattern appears at the end of the string.

nodes.name: Regex Find All
nodes.description:
Finds all non-overlapping matches of a regular expression pattern in the string, returning a list of the matched substrings.

Each item carries `start` and `end` byte-offset attributes pointing into the original string.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to search within.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The regular expression pattern to search for.

inputs.name: case_insensitive
inputs.description: Match letters regardless of case.

inputs.name: multiline
inputs.description: Make `^` and `$` match the start and end of each line, not just the whole string.

nodes.name: Regex Replace
nodes.description: Replaces matches of a regular expression pattern in the string. The replacement string can reference captures: `$0` for the whole match and `$1`, `$2`, etc. for capture groups.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The regular expression pattern to search for.

inputs.name: replacement
inputs.description: The replacement string. Use `$0` for the whole match and `$1`, `$2`, etc. for capture groups.

inputs.name: replace_all
inputs.description: Replace all matches. When disabled, only the first match is replaced.

inputs.name: case_insensitive
inputs.description: Match letters regardless of case.

inputs.name: multiline
inputs.description: Make `^` and `$` match the start and end of each line, not just the whole string.

nodes.name: Regex Split
nodes.description:
Splits a string into a list of substrings pulled from between separator characters as matched by a regular expression.

For example, splitting "Three, two, one... LIFTOFF" with pattern `\W+` (non-word characters) produces `["Three", "two", "one", "LIFTOFF"]`.

inputs.name: string
inputs.description: The string to split into substrings.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: The regular expression pattern to split on. Matches are consumed and not included in the output.

inputs.name: case_insensitive
inputs.description: Match letters regardless of case.

inputs.name: multiline
inputs.description: Make `^` and `$` match the start and end of each line, not just the whole string.

nodes.name: Bool Value
nodes.description: Constructs a bool value which may be set to true or false.

nodes.name: Color Value
nodes.description: Constructs a color value which may be set to any color, or no color.

nodes.name: Footprint Value
nodes.description: Constructs a footprint value which may be set to any transformation of a unit square describing a render area, and a render resolution at least 1x1 integer pixels.

nodes.name: Gradient Value
nodes.description: Constructs a gradient value which may be set to any sequence of color stops to represent the transition between colors.

nodes.name: Number Value
nodes.description: Constructs a number value which may be set to any real number.

nodes.name: Percentage Value
nodes.description: Constructs a number value which may be set to any value from 0% to 100% by dragging the slider.

nodes.name: String Value
nodes.description: Constructs a string value which may be set to any plain text.

nodes.name: Vec2 Value
nodes.description: Constructs a two-dimensional vector value which may be set to any XY pair.

nodes.name: Apply Transform
nodes.description: Applies the vector path's local transformation to its geometry and resets the transform to the identity.

nodes.name: As Vector
nodes.description: Type-asserts a value to be vector data.

nodes.name: Flatten Vector
nodes.description: Converts a `Graphic[]` into a `Vector[]` by deeply flattening any vector content it contains, and discarding any non-vector content.

nodes.name: Points to Polyline
nodes.description: Creates a polyline from a series of vector points, replacing any existing segments and regions that may already exist.

nodes.name: Index Points
nodes.description:
Retrieves the vec2 position (in local space) of the anchor point at the specified index in a `List` of vector elements.
If no value exists at that index, the position (0, 0) is returned.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The vector element or elements containing the anchor points to be retrieved.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the points to retrieve, starting from 0 for the first point. Negative indices count backwards from the end, starting from -1 for the last item.

nodes.name: Path is Closed
nodes.description: Determines if the subpath at the given index (across all vector element subpaths) is closed, meaning its ends are connected together forming a loop.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The vector content whose subpaths are inspected.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The index of the subpath to check, counting across subpaths in all vector elements.

nodes.name: Position on Path
nodes.description:
Determines the position of a point on the path, given by its progression from 0 to 1 along the path.

If multiple subpaths make up the path, the whole number part of the progression value selects the subpath and the decimal part determines the position along it.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The path to traverse.

inputs.name: progression
inputs.description: The factor from the start to the end of the path, 0–1 for one subpath, 1–2 for a second subpath, and so on.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Swap the direction of the path.

inputs.name: parameterized_distance
inputs.description: Traverse the path using each segment's Bézier curve parameterization instead of the Euclidean distance. Faster to compute but doesn't respect actual distances.

nodes.name: Tangent on Path
nodes.description:
Determines the angle of the tangent at a point on the path, given by its progression from 0 to 1 along the path.

If multiple subpaths make up the path, the whole number part of the progression value selects the subpath and the decimal part determines the position along it.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The path to traverse.

inputs.name: progression
inputs.description: The factor from the start to the end of the path, 0–1 for one subpath, 1–2 for a second subpath, and so on.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Swap the direction of the path.

inputs.name: parameterized_distance
inputs.description: Traverse the path using each segment's Bézier curve parameterization instead of the Euclidean distance. Faster to compute but doesn't respect actual distances.

inputs.name: radians
inputs.description: Whether the resulting angle should be given in as radians instead of degrees.

nodes.name: Auto-Tangents
nodes.description: Automatically constructs tangents (Bézier handles) for anchor points in a vector path.

inputs.name: spread
inputs.description: The amount of spread for the auto-tangents, from 0 (sharp corner) to 1 (full spread).

inputs.name: preserve_existing
inputs.description: If active, existing non-zero handles won't be affected.

nodes.name: Boolean Operation
nodes.description: Combines the geometric forms of one or more closed paths into a new vector path that results from cutting or joining the paths by the chosen method.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The `List` of vector paths to perform the boolean operation on. Nested `List`s are automatically flattened.

inputs.name: operation
inputs.description:
Which boolean operation to perform on the paths.
Union combines all paths while cutting out overlapping areas (even the interiors of a single path).
Subtraction cuts overlapping areas out from the last (Subtract Front) or first (Subtract Back) path.
Intersection cuts away all but the overlapping areas shared by every path.
Difference cuts away the overlapping areas shared by every path, leaving only the non-overlapping areas.

nodes.name: Cut Path
nodes.description:
Cuts a path at a given progression from 0 to 1 along the path, creating two new subpaths from the original one (if the path is initially open) or one open subpath (if the path is initially closed).

If multiple subpaths make up the path, the whole number part of the progression value selects the subpath and the decimal part determines the position along it.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The path to insert a cut into.

inputs.name: progression
inputs.description: The factor from the start to the end of the path, 0–1 for one subpath, 1–2 for a second subpath, and so on.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Swap the direction of the path.

inputs.name: parameterized_distance
inputs.description: Traverse the path using each segment's Bézier curve parameterization instead of the Euclidean distance. Faster to compute but doesn't respect actual distances.

nodes.name: Cut Segments
nodes.description: Cuts path segments into separate disconnected pieces where each is a distinct subpath.

nodes.name: Decimate
nodes.description: Decimates vector paths into polylines by sampling any curves into line segments, then removing points that don't significantly contribute to the shape using the Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The vector paths to decimate.

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.description: The maximum distance a point can deviate from the simplified path before it is kept.

nodes.name: Jitter Points
nodes.description: Perturbs the positions of anchor points in vector geometry by random amounts and directions.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The vector geometry with points to be jittered.

inputs.name: max_distance
inputs.description: The maximum extent of the random distance each point can be offset.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Seed used to determine unique variations on all randomized offsets.

inputs.name: along_normals
inputs.description: Whether to offset anchor points along their normal direction (perpendicular to the path) or in a random direction. Free-floating and branching points have no normal direction, so they receive a random-angled offset regardless of this setting.

nodes.name: Morph
nodes.description:
Interpolates the geometry, appearance, and transform between multiple vector layers, producing a single morphed vector shape.

*Progression* morphs through all objects. Interpolation is linear unless *Path* geometry is provided to control the trajectory between key objects. The **Origins to Polyline** node may be used to create a path with anchor points corresponding to each object. Other nodes can modify its path segments.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The vector objects to interpolate between. Mixed graphic content is deeply flattened to keep only vector elements.

nodes.name: Offset Points
nodes.description:
Displaces anchor points along their normal direction (perpendicular to the path) by a set distance.
Points with 0 or 3+ segment connections have no well-defined normal and are left in place.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The vector geometry with points to be offset.

inputs.name: distance
inputs.description: The distance to offset each anchor point along its normal. Positive values move outward, negative values move inward.

nodes.name: Sample Polyline
nodes.description: Convert vector geometry into a polyline composed of evenly spaced points.

nodes.name: Simplify
nodes.description: Simplifies vector paths by reducing the number of curve segments while preserving the overall shape within the given tolerance.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The vector paths to simplify.

inputs.name: tolerance
inputs.description: The maximum distance the simplified path may deviate from the original.

nodes.name: Arc
nodes.description: Generates an arc shape forming a portion of a circle which may be open, closed, or a pie slice.

nodes.name: Arrow
nodes.description: Generates an arrow from the origin to the chosen coordinate.

nodes.name: Circle
nodes.description: Generates a circle shape with a chosen radius.

nodes.name: Ellipse
nodes.description: Generates an ellipse shape (an oval or stretched circle) with the chosen radii.

nodes.name: Grid
nodes.description: Generates a rectangular or isometric grid with the chosen number of columns and rows. Line segments connect the points, forming a vector mesh.

nodes.name: QR Code
nodes.description: Generates a QR code from the input text.

nodes.name: Rectangle
nodes.description: Generates a rectangle shape with the chosen width and height. It may also have rounded corners if desired.

inputs.name: _individual_corner_radii
inputs.rust_type: bool, // TODO: Move this to the bottom once we have a migration capability

nodes.name: Regular Polygon
nodes.description: Generates an regular polygon shape like a triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, or any higher n-gon.

nodes.name: Spiral
nodes.description: Generates a spiral shape that winds from an inner to an outer radius.

nodes.name: Star
nodes.description: Generates an n-pointed star shape with inner and outer points at chosen radii from the center.

nodes.name: Assign Colors
nodes.description: Uniquely sets the fill and/or stroke style of every vector element to individual colors sampled along a chosen gradient.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The content with vector paths to apply the fill and/or stroke style to.

inputs.name: fill
inputs.description: Whether to style the fill.

inputs.name: stroke
inputs.description: Whether to style the stroke.

inputs.name: gradient
inputs.description: The range of colors to select from.

inputs.name: reverse
inputs.description: Whether to reverse the gradient.

inputs.name: randomize
inputs.description: Whether to randomize the color selection for each element from throughout the gradient.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description:
The seed used for randomization.
Seed to determine unique variations on the randomized color selection.

inputs.name: repeat_every
inputs.description: The number of elements to span across the gradient before repeating. A 0 value will span the entire gradient once.

nodes.name: Fill
nodes.description: Applies a fill style to the vector content, giving an appearance to the area within the interior of the geometry.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The content with vector paths to apply the fill style to.

inputs.name: fill
inputs.description: The fill to paint the path with.

nodes.name: Stroke
nodes.description: Applies a stroke style to the vector content, giving an appearance to the area within the outline of the geometry.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The content with vector paths to apply the stroke style to.

inputs.name: paint
inputs.description: The stroke paint.

inputs.name: weight
inputs.description: The stroke thickness.

inputs.name: align
inputs.description: The alignment of stroke to the path's centerline or (for closed shapes) the inside or outside of the shape.

inputs.name: cap
inputs.description: The shape of the stroke at open endpoints.

inputs.name: join
inputs.description: The curvature of the bent stroke at sharp corners.

inputs.name: miter_limit
inputs.description: The threshold for when a miter-joined stroke is converted to a bevel-joined stroke when a sharp angle becomes pointier than this ratio.

inputs.name: paint_order
inputs.description: The order to paint the stroke on top of the fill, or the fill on top of the stroke.

inputs.name: dash_lengths
inputs.description: The stroke dash lengths. Each length forms a distance in a pattern where the first length is a dash, the second is a gap, and so on. If the list is an odd length, the pattern repeats with solid-gap roles reversed.

inputs.name: dash_offset
inputs.description: The phase offset distance from the starting point of the dash pattern.

nodes.name: Decode Image
nodes.description:
Converts raw binary data to a raster image.

Works with standard image format (PNG, JPEG, WebP, etc.). Automatically converts the color space to linear sRGB for accurate compositing.

nodes.name: Get Request
nodes.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to a specified URL and optionally waits for the response (unless discarded) which is output as a string.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The web address to send the GET request to.

inputs.name: discard_result
inputs.description: Makes the request run in the background without waiting on a response. This is useful for triggering webhooks without blocking the continued execution of the graph.

nodes.name: Image to Bytes
nodes.description: Converts extracted raw RGBA pixel data from an input image. Each pixel becomes 4 sequential bytes. Useful for transmission over HTTP or writing to files.

nodes.name: Load Resource
nodes.description: Loads binary from URLs and local asset paths. Returns a transparent placeholder if the resource fails to load, allowing rendering to continue.

nodes.name: Post Request
nodes.description: Sends an HTTP POST request to a specified URL with the provided binary data and optionally waits for the response (unless discarded) which is output as a string.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: The web address to send the POST request to.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: The binary data to include in the body of the POST request.

inputs.name: discard_result
inputs.description: Makes the request run in the background without waiting on a response. This is useful for triggering webhooks without blocking the continued execution of the graph.

nodes.name: String to Bytes
nodes.description: Converts a text string to raw binary data. Useful for transmission over HTTP or writing to files.
